- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in the recent history, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for the next 5–10 days.
- If model shows a sharp upward trend (e.g., >0.5% daily increase) followed by a spike, it often overestimates later; cap forecast at 1–2% above peak or apply a 1–3 day decay.
- When true outcome shows a strong upward move (e.g., >5% from prior 10-day avg), model often lags; add 1–2 days of lagged momentum to forecast.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.0), model tends to overpredict; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- Model often underestimates the “mean reversion” phase after a spike; if true outcome shows a sharp rise followed by decline, forecast should curve downward after peak.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently misses the “late-cycle” dip (last 5–7 days); add a 1–2% downward bias in final 5–7 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.20 spikes, model tends to overreact; apply a 0.5–1.0% dampening factor to forecast slope.
